responses.title: The Button Sorting Switch
story: Think of the box as a mail sorter. Each time you press a button, the remote sends a secret number. Just before this part of the code, the box catches that number and keeps it. Now it has to decide what to do with it.

Line 169 starts a switch. A switch looks at the number and jumps to the matching case, like a mail sorter dropping a letter into the right slot. Up, down, left and right each move the turret one small step.

OK fires one dart. Star fires all six darts. Button 1 makes the turret nod yes, and button 2 makes it shake no. Each case ends with break, which means 'done, leave the sorter'. If no case matches, nothing happens.

steps.label: Read the button
steps.detail: The switch looks at the command number the remote just sent and picks the matching case.

steps.label: Tilt buttons
steps.detail: Up and down call helpers that tilt the barrel one small step each press.

steps.label: Turn buttons
steps.detail: Left and right call helpers that spin the whole turret a short, timed burst.

steps.label: Fire one
steps.detail: OK calls fire(), which spins the drum just enough to launch a single dart.

steps.label: Fire all
steps.detail: Star calls fireAll(), which spins the drum six times as long to launch every dart.

steps.label: Nod and shake
steps.detail: Button 1 nods yes and button 2 shakes no, three times each.

responses.metaphor: The switch is like a mail sorter that reads a number on each letter and drops it into the right slot.
responses.watch_for: Press OK and count one dart, then press star and see if all six go; a button with no case, like 5, should do nothing.
